column3: Locale namespace manifest for ui-conversation: only meta.title = "ui-conversation".
Chinese locale manifest: meta.title "会话界面框架" plus a description string.
Package manifest: version 0.2.1-rc.2, client inject list, Lexical/React deps, export map for "." "./client" and "./src/*".
Per-heading bilingual hash record for README.md; names the `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing --write` regeneration command.

Package reference: the whole Conversation-assembly contract, sent-user-text rules, shell/standard props, temporary composer entries, and the explicit "Model Experience: none / KV Cache effect: none" statement.
Chinese translation of the package reference; same section set, kept in sync by the hash record.

Plugin entry: registers the assembly, the user-text factory, the Enter-behaviour setting row, fixed keyboard commands, the File action, the input hub, and every shell slot; owns Workspace-navigation draft transfer.
Derives the bounded context-occupancy triple (percent, usedTokens, contextWindow) from the token-meter pressure projection; returns null until both numerator and capacity exist.
Type contract for the per-session composer block: a localized reason plus the registry face other plugins reach through ctx.conversation.blocks.
Submission vocabulary: InputSubmitMode, the enter/accelerated gesture, and the frozen MessageSubmission occurrence (timestamp, source, mode, session/model/run-mode snapshot).
Context-role vocabulary ('inject' | 'recall') and the known durable context forms the UI knows how to present; unknown forms stay opaque.
The Definition/Builder contract: match/start/update, exclusive claims, location data, incremental replace/apply builders, and conversationContextKey's length-prefixed collision-free key.
Editor-facing contract: TokenSpan (revision-guarded), ReferenceInsert, DraftSnapshot (persisted semantic document), ComposerKeyboard, and the Occurrence projection.
Grouping contract: GroupUpdate (replace vs apply), GroupSnapshot, NodeReference/RenderEntry, and the ConversationGroupDefinition input surface.
The frozen input contract: InputState currency, InputEvent/InputEffect union, CommandClaim, InputTarget scoped verbs, and the SubmitAttempt identity that makes stale settles droppable.
Every finalized transcript node type (user, assistant, steering, context, model-retry, turn-error, turn-max-tokens, tool-result, command, compaction, unknown) and the lazy ToolArgs view.

Request-header interpretation: ConversationPromptSnapshot, SystemPromptNode, RequestPromptChange kinds anchored at the event that introduced the change, and inspectRequestPrompt's canonicalization/classifier.
Every slot this package owns (composer chain, input docks, view tabs, images, user text) plus the composed prop types and the three-tier standard-props contract.
Target-neutral ConversationSnapshot and conversationPhase(), which derives blank/engaging/active from Session lifecycle plus the active-target set.

Immutable system-surface interpretation: inspectSystemPrompt keeps loaded system nodes in surface order, maps positional replacements, and withholds the prompt when the older endpoint order is unknown.
User-text rule contract: forward matchers over original text, the synchronous Facts reader, and the JSON-only node shape.
View tab, one-shot focus request, and the per-session ConversationStoreState (draft, selected view, pending view request).

The incremental assembly engine: Context lifecycle, exclusive claims resolved before any acceptance (so the outcome is order-independent and an ambiguous claim throws), the per-context dependency map that drives replay when older history arrives, assistant-settlement retirement, and replace/prepend/append paths.
Per-Session binding: window revision handling, three-frame animation-frame publication, target activation, the image-URL cache face, and the system/request prompt inspection seams.
Shared registry base: reference-stable ordered entries, effect-owned registration, idempotent disposers, and synchronous invalidation on change.
Event Definition registry: callable or table-form matchers, precomputed per-type candidate sets, the single unmatched-event fallback, and the target/buildViewNode pairing rule.
One optional Group Definition per existing view target; registration never instantiates a builder and rejects an unknown target.
Atomic group publication: validates the whole batch (one-to-one root/group correspondence, no overlapping rendering positions) before installing it and reuses unchanged references.
Session-scoped durable image URL cache: one read and one browser URL per attachment, seeded previews replaced by canonical bytes, and object URLs revoked with the session scope.
Turn/Step timeline index: coordinates per event, incremental boundary append, reference-stable Turn/Step locations, and per-key Location-data stores.
Per-document candidate reconciliation: earliest-start wins, per-matcher query caching keyed by offset, tracked Fact dependencies, and JSON identity reuse across evaluations.
Rule registry: reserved/empty/duplicate ID rejection, deterministic (order, id) sorting, and a monotonic revision the renderer subscribes to.
Per-target view-builder registry; one definition per target, effect-owned lifetime.
Semantic draft snapshots: zod-validated persistence shape (ordered non-overlapping reference spans after the command token), plus copy/export helpers.
Attachment error copy: user-solvable Host rejection reasons map to limit-naming copy, unsolvable ones fold into one send-failed line carrying the reason code.
Package public surface: exports the assembly, registries, contracts and the UserTextDataMap/UserTextFacts declaration merges; declares the cordis `conversation` and `uiConversation` context faces.
ComposerBlockRegistry: the one way another plugin makes a session's input inert, carrying the blocker's own localized reason.
Plain-text reference scan: a /name or @name token on the trigger lexicon plus syntax-recognizable @dir/ folder tokens, with strict lexical boundaries.
ReferenceChipNode: one atomic Lexical decorator per reference; NodeKey carries identity, the node caches the owner's display projections, and getTextContent answers the clipboard form.
CommandChipNode: the claimed slash command as an atomic decorator carrying its claim, plus the seat transform that releases the claim when text lands before the chip.
Two-step chip deletion: the first Backspace/Delete selects the chip, the second removes it, and any other key, click, or blur clears the selection.
Pure visual body of the command chip (icon-free label span reusing the reference chip's treatment).
Shared inline-reference CSS: padding/radius that does not change text metrics, hover tint, and the selected-command-chip tint.
The composer's contenteditable host: binds the shell-owned editor to a resident div and reflects the `editable` prop, so the no-session state is the same DOM inert.
Portal loop that renders each decorator node's React face into its host element, keyed by NodeKey so chip DOM identity survives text edits.
Stateless presentation of the scrollport, editable surface, placeholder, and chip portals; owns no Hooks.
Composer keymap at CRITICAL priority: menu arbitration, space adjudication, the Enter submit gesture, IME composition guards, and paste routing to file intake.
Three pure text views of one editor state: detectText (chip = one U+FFFC), clipboardText (chip expanded), and the occurrence view, plus the point→offset folding.
Routes composer clicks on chips and editable text-refs to the reference owner without changing the draft; a double-click's first click already opens.
Chip metrics: inline-flex, 240px max width, ellipsized label, and the error-colored invalid treatment.
Pure visual body of one reference chip: domain glyph or trigger marker plus the label, with the invalid bit styled.
The shell-owned Lexical editor: plain-text/history registration, selection preservation, draft set/paste/restore/clear operations, and the reference-placeholder sanitizer.
The one place a numeric TokenSpan is mapped back onto Lexical points and applied; atomic segments resolve to element points so a span can only address a chip whole.
TextRefNode: a lexicon-matched /name token as an editable text entity (not a chip) that re-evaluates its match shape on every edit.
DOM and keymap wiring owned by the InputBar: focus with reveal, edge-of-draft wheel chaining, the file-picker binding, and the keymap's live gate.
SessionInput shell: owns the editor and the pure SubmitMachine, and choreographs claims, adjudication, the default sink, chip serialization, the notice channel, and draft persistence.
Session-bound input registry: one shell per retained binding, the scoped slash-event listeners, the catalogue subscription, and the default-send/steer-queue choreography.

The pure submit-plane state machine: plain/claimed/adjudicating/submitting phases, the single frozen command slot, ordinary sends detached at Enter so the editor clears immediately, and stale-attempt rejection by attempt seq.
Reports the original message occurrence to product analytics with the captured session/model/run-mode snapshot, not newer session facts.
Resolves a submit gesture into queue/steer delivery and owns the live busy-Enter preference (local store + Host settings write).
The `conversation` namespace dictionary: zh is the key-set source of truth, en is checked complete against it, and the type union is derived from zh.
Queue strip CSS: dock inset geometry, the panel that reads as one surface with the input card, and the row/action states.
Queue strip: durable inbox rows plus local submission echoes, edit/remove/steer actions, durable thumbnails, and the UserText preview with whitespace collapsed and CSS ellipsis.
Scope-addressed Conversation service: send, sendSession with the submission echo, background file-upload queue with bounded concurrency, draft attachments, and queue operations.
Settings row CSS for the busy-Enter selector: title/description column plus a pill button.
General-Settings row exposing the busy-Enter preference (Queue/Steer) through a menu.
Context ring and breakdown-panel CSS: the ring, the segmented bar, the swatch colors, and the `.headline:empty` collapse for locales.
Context-occupancy control: a ring and percentage below the composer plus a click-open breakdown of system/tools/messages, with locale-owned word order.
Measures the composer's control groups and sets `data-model-compact` when the expanded controls cannot share a line.
The shared Conversation body: workspace chip resolution, the hero/composer chain, the sticky composer seat, and the inert-vs-blocked-vs-hero composer postures.
Resident header: keeps global navigation without a Session and renders the strict Session header only when one exists.
Main frame: derives the settling/hero/active phase from Session open state and the list summary, and renders the content factory with the width controls.
Root-scoped main occupant that renders the `main.conversation` slot.
Shell CSS: header rows, crumb trail, view tabs, transcript scrollport, sticky composer seat, and the width drag handles.
Resident Conversation skeleton; the composer bar stays mounted across no-session/session transitions.
Strict per-Session header (breadcrumbs, actions, utilities, view tabs) and the Session body that renders the active view.
Transcript content-width drag handles with a persisted localStorage preference, a minimum width, and wheel forwarding to the scrollport.
Renders the active view, binds draft persistence for the Session, and returns null while the Session is still blank.
Hero chrome: the workspace chip, the headline, and the SMIL-morphing fish logo; the composer itself stays in ConversationRoot.
Hero CSS: the centered stack, overflow-driven headline wrap, the preview badge, and the reduced-motion-guarded swim animation.
Composer CSS: the card, the single scrollport, the placeholder, the control row with the model-collapse state, and the primary/send/stop buttons.
The default composer: the Lexical draft surface, attachment rail, control row, primary Send/Stop seat whose label names the delivery mode, and the toast/notice channels.
Safari-only detection and layout repair for the composer textarea and its scrollport.
Todo dock CSS: the shared dock inset geometry, the menu surface, and the single-line ellipsized item text.
Todo dock: reads the host-computed todos projection, renders per-status markers, and collapses to a per-status count summary.
Two-independent-Escape stop sequence: the first press is short-lived and cleared before an accepted cancellation runs.
Routes the fixed Escape input into the current turn's scoped cancellation, excluding terminal/iframe/approval/inert regions and resetting on lifecycle changes.
Per-Session Conversation store (draft, view, view request) plus localStorage readers that tolerate absent, malformed, and legacy records.
User-text rule that folds the wire `@[label](dsh-session:id)` form and bare session labels into a session node.
UserText CSS: `display: contents` inline by default, and the single-line ellipsis variant.
Presentation of user text: evaluates through the data layer, renders each JSON node through the keyed slot, and keeps the original text on a rule failure.
Two whitespace rules (collapse runs, trim document edges) that share the same cursor/priority/Facts cache as reference rules.
Deterministic view selection: the registered preference wins, then `chat`, and never an arbitrary first view.
Ambient declaration for `*.module.css` (a Record of class names) and bare `*.css` imports.
Host-side entry: the schemastery `busyEnter` preference projected to the browser and the settings-page exclusion.
Host-side schema for the busy-Enter preference: namespace, field, allowed values, default, and the durable wire envelope.
End-to-end plugin-API tests: the File action, the target-neutral read face, Inspect availability, View activation, draft mirroring, and Workspace draft transfer with structured references.
Slot-wiring tests: developer-tools hides only Trajectory, the subtree waits for the layout declaration, the services install without Chat, and the store is shared by body and header.
Acceptance tests for the assembled surfaces: the inert no-Session state, the same textarea DOM across blank→active, the promptError strip, and the title projection.
Late insertions preserve surrounding references, undo ownership, and reject a stale revision or a disposed editor.
ComposerBlockRegistry republishes only when the localized copy changes.
Host plugin registers, validates, and disposes the durable busy-Enter preference and keeps itself off the generated Settings pages.
ContextMeter tests: nothing renders until pressure and capacity are known, the ring and panel open, locales own the headline order, and zero occupancy draws no segment.
jsdom shim: replaces document.fonts with a bare EventTarget so the layout test drives its own font-loading events.
Control-row measurement tests: collapse on expanded demand, remeasure on text change and font load, and full observer disconnection.
The assembler's contract in 44 cases plus two parameterised tables: Context lifecycle, Location repair, dependency replay, exclusive claims, settlement retirement, prepend repair, and loud failures.
Group store tests: one changed group publishes without touching root or member identities, references move atomically, and complete replacement re-validates.
Group Definition dispatch tests: builder created only on first activation, lifecycle changes without upserts, rebuild, removal, and the required complete grouping for replacement input.
Registry tests: open-turn publication without a view, three-frame publication, duplicate rejection, disposal with the caller fiber, and rebuild coalescing.
Event-routing tests: mixed function and table routes in registration order, table-only dispatch per payload, receiver preservation, and fallback normalization.
Store tests: per-Session persistence, independent live instances, structured-reference restore, legacy string drafts, and every unusable saved-record shape.

Draft-document tests: copy independence, reference export, persisted decoding, command-chip rebuild after the catalogue resolves, revision-stable snapshots, and failed-send restoration in submission order.
InputHub tests: catalogue subscription rides lifecycle activation, the shell is reused, the initial draft is restored before return, and disposal unsubscribes.
Focus-preservation tests: background insertion and undo stay outside the editor until focus is explicitly restored.
Settings-row tests: the busy-only scope copy, Queue by default, live preference changes, and outside-close.
Image-cache tests: a pending load is invalidated when the binding is released, a seeded preview is replaced by canonical bytes and both URLs revoked.
Opt-in synthetic benchmark comparing raw vs v2-compacted Assistant stream history: bytes, gzip/brotli, host and client heap peaks, and exact replay equivalence.
Attachment-rejection copy tests: megabyte formatting, user-solvable reasons mapped to limit copy, and unknown reasons folded into the send-failed line.
The composer's full behavioural contract: focus handoff, placeholders, the attachment rail, Enter semantics, running/lock states, the send label, decorations, and the claim chip.
A state matrix over the input machine: plain, claimed, claimed-with-attachments, submitting, locked, and takeover, each with its admitted and refused edits.
Reference submission and submit-transaction hardening: canonical mirror text, retained chips on failure, abort on disposal, and one image-only prompt per settlement.
End-to-end scenarios through the real pipeline: menu-pick claims, pasted slash lines, execute-kind commands, chip deletion semantics, and unknown-slash fallback.
Keymap routing tests: composition presentation is cleared on root swap, Enter routes to submit, and Tab arbitrates or passes.
Editor-core tests: ReferenceChipNode and CommandChipNode JSON round-trips, the three projections, detect-offset folding, and span application across paragraphs and chips.
QueueDock tests: empty rendering, local echo handoff by rpcId, collapsing headers, inline editing, steering, thumbnails, and error notices.
Chip and text-ref activation opens the owner once, leaves selections alone, and refuses invalid chips.
ReferenceChip renders the domain icon, the trigger-marker fallback, and the invalid styling bit.
inspectRequestPrompt tests: initial vs resume headers, system/tool/combined change classification, an emptied prompt, and an in-history update that reports no system change.
Safari detection and textarea layout-repair tests, including the absent-textarea teardown case.
The Conversation store seat is shared between body and header, isolated per Session, and recreated with its persisted state after scope disposal.
ConversationController tests: scoped routing, failure folding, steer convergence, upload bounding and cancellation, the submission echo lifecycle, and image dimension probing.
Shell tests: hero chrome, the resident composer, subagent breadcrumbs, the settling phase, the sticky seat, the width handles, and the promptError strip.
Stop-sequence tests: two independent presses inside the interval, the inclusive endpoint, expiry, and invalidation.
Stop-shortcut tests: two eligible Escapes, resets on other keys/modals, exclusion of terminal/iframe/approval/inert regions, and per-lifecycle invalidation.
Submit-mode resolution and the busy-Enter preference: local publish before the durable write, host adoption without write-back.
The submit machine's whole state table: plain/claimed/adjudicating/submitting, claim release and re-entry, rollback, anti-backwash, and per-session isolation.
System-surface tests: unknown replacement order withholds the prompt, compaction restores A, chained replacements use surface order, and empty tails are ignored.
TodoPanel and TodoDock tests: empty rendering, collapsed summary, per-status markers, parallel active counting, and the host-projection wiring.
Shared React fixture that mounts the user-text factory with a rule set and facts for the component tests.
Competition between reference rules: an earlier complete file beats a session label, quoted paths stay whole, and only the changed matcher is re-queried.
Registry tests: every matcher is queried, JSON identity is reused across key order, reserved/duplicate IDs are rejected, and rules die with their fiber.
Candidate-scheduling tests: consumed heads advance, cached queries are reused, changed matchers replay alone, failures cache at their exact offset, and reentrancy is rejected.
Whitespace-rule tests: edge collisions favour trim, only the switch reader is refreshed, and no second run is invented inside a consumed run.
UserText projection tests: complete original text is retained, a matching failure is reported once, wire session forms fold to a label, and text-selection gestures survive.
resolveActiveView prefers the registered selection, then chat, and never an arbitrary view.
Compile-time negative samples for the view-ring types plus a runtime check that a registered View projects tabs and disposes through the slot ledger.
CSS assertions that the width handle's gutter hit target stays narrow, the hover indicator compact, and the indicator above the composer during capture.

Client tsconfig: rootDir src, outDir lib/types, and 32 project references (api, session-controller, workspace-controller, attachment, brand, ui-*, llm, session, plan-mode, goal, tool-todo, settings, file-reference, shortcuts, analytics); excludes src/index.ts so the Host entry stays out of the browser build.
Host tsconfig covering only src/submission-settings.ts and src/index.ts, referencing cordis, schemastery, and the settings package.
Solution tsconfig referencing the host and client projects.
Bundle config: the shared clientBundle helper with the type entry as the extra output.
Locale namespace manifest for ui-tool: only meta.title = "ui-tool".
Chinese locale manifest: meta.title "工具调用展示" plus a description string.
Package manifest: client inject list, the ui-primitives/ui-slots/test-runtime dev deps, and the export map for "." "./client" and "./src/*".
Per-heading bilingual hash record for the ui-tool README and the regeneration command.
Package reference: the keyed per-tool-view dispatch rule, the built-in views, the rendering contract, the card models, and the declared optional capabilities.
Chinese translation of the package reference.
Registers the Tool call tree on the `conversation.chat.node` slot and mounts every built-in atomic toolview.
Tool slot declarations: the keyed `tool.call.toolview`, the `tool.call.images` child slot, the phase-specific owner props, and the optional UserQuestionPanels capability.
Browser entry: exports apply/inject and the Tool slot prop types.
Exports the `conversation` locale namespace constant reused by every Tool renderer.
CSS for the call row and the nested sub-call container.
Root/subcall composition: memoized branches, one keyed atomic dispatch path, the Auto-denial bypass, and the stable `call:<id>` DOM anchors.
Ask-question transcript CSS: the item list, the answer lines, the skipped treatment, and the verdict line.
Renders a validated ask-user transcript as an answered definition list or an unanswered question list.
CSS for the neutral exit-status capsule and its failure dot.
Neutral capsule showing only the recorded exit code, signal, or missing-code status.
CSS for the question row's answer-panel button.
Question-owned summary action and transcript disclosure; the panel button owns its own click and keyboard handling.
Detail-body CSS: item rows, status and change markers, badges with tone colors, field lists, nested groups, and the path button.
Compact read-only renderer for recorded Tool results: fields, badges, markdown, code, locations, nested groups, and the unchanged-items disclosure.
Tool-row CSS: the leading slot, the title, the ellipsized summary, the unshrunk summary suffix, the diff totals, the IO card, and the visually hidden status text.
The shared tool row: disclosure chrome, the mutually exclusive card slots, the file link vs URL link vs plain summary, the exit capsule, and the Inspect pill.
Plain, locale-free card data for the ask-user transcript: answered or unanswered, with a skipped label.
Normalizes an Auto-review denial reason for display only (trim, collapse line separators) and localizes the collapsed and expanded copy.
Entity lists and receipts for agent, job, terminal, and LSP tools, parsed from the producers' own text formats.
Shared detail vocabulary: JSON narrowing, the status-to-badge map, the field-label map, and the recursive inspection-item projection with a depth cap.
Compact detail bodies for todo, goal, and schedule results, with the schedule frequency vocabulary and the local-time-zone date formatting.
Diff-card derivation: the intended diff from write/edit/str_replace arguments, the applied diff from result metadata, and the decision to fall back to the intended diff.
Image-card derivation: the references come from the result's own image blocks, the path from the metadata, and any block the card cannot render declines the whole card.
Recorded inspection, session-query, trace, and workflow/Ralph report bodies; a spilled result stays generic.
Localized label adapters that bind the shared UI primitives' label surfaces to the conversation dictionary.
Narrowing helpers for raw tool calls: a WeakMap-cached argument parse and the single-text-block result reader.

Read-card derivation from the persisted metadata plus the model-facing envelope, the call's 1-based start line (read from the arguments so it works while the call runs), and the chat row's 8-line resident body cap.
Reads one operation-time absolute path from opaque persisted result metadata.
Search-card derivation for grep/glob from the persisted metadata, including the capped-result recovery text.
Terminal-card derivation: shell and terminal-send calls, the exit-status marker parse, the workdir normalisation, and the persistent/spilled/background paths that stay generic.
Todo change summary against the recorded predecessor list: added, updated, moved, and removed items.
Indexes the recorded todo writes and the predecessor list of each todo call, published as a `tool-todo-history` view target.

The row-model core: tool-name classification and titles (cordis_define is deliberately absent because a keyed hit replaces the generic row), the argument summary, the file-path rules, the result flattening, the state derivation, and the Auto-denial identity.
Web-card derivation for web_search and web_fetch from the persisted metadata, plus the safe http(s) href reader.
The ask-user row: pairs questions with answers by id, reads the projections for late replies, and exposes the reopen/review panel verbs.
Bash-row CSS: the idle/hover chevron swap, the title/summary line, the IO card, and the inspect pill.
The bash/pwsh row: terminal card when available, generic IO for failures, persistent shells, spills, and background launches, with a keyboard-toggleable row.
One row component registered for exactly 37 recorded-result tool names, with the icon chosen by tool-name family and the LSP operation-specific title.
Write/edit row: the decoded-input size in KB computed from the lazy argument view, plus the diff card.
The dispatch fallback: classifies the tool, derives every card model, and turns a failing terminal exit into the row's error state.
Derives the todo row's done/total counts and the first active item, with the extra active count kept out of the truncating text.
Shared assembly for the read and read_image rows: one chrome, one result-side card.
The read_image row: the durable image as the card body, dispatched through the tool-owned image slot, with a text fallback for every non-image shape.
The read row: the read card plus the call's start line so the path opens where the model looked.
The grep/glob row: the search card, the error summary, and the per-tool titles.
The todo_write row: the plan summary, the diff against the recorded predecessor, and the injected todo-history target.
The web_search/web_fetch row: the web card and the http(s) href that opens in a new tab.
Ambient declaration for `*.module.css` in the ui-tool package.
Host loader entry for the browser-only Tool plugin; provides no host-side behavior.
The ask-question row's whole state table: waiting, pending, crash-repaired, late-replied, cancelled, aborted, and window-truncated results.
Assembly acceptance: the todo_write row and plan strip, and the terminal card reached through both the keyed bash row and the generic fallback.
run_code sub-calls through the real chat machinery: nested rows, the program body, error state parity, file opening, and running dispatch nesting.
Presentation tails: the stopped state keeps the business icon, the others-variant sparkle icon, and the bash row's non-clickable summary.
Detail-model tests: JSON narrowing, status localization, depth and size limits, the control adapters, the inspection adapters, and the generic fallback contract.
Goal, reminder, and todo detail bodies, the keyboard-expanding detail row, the teammate icon family, and the keyed registration.
Diff-card tests: the intended vs applied diff, the str_replace_editor cases, the malformed-metadata fallbacks, and the FileMutationRow presentation.
Image-card tests: the metadata/envelope derivation, the post-execute-hook case, every decline path, and the read_image row's slot dispatch.
Preparing rows: a file row survives streamed arguments, dispatch, and result, the edit size updates as the strings cross a kilobyte, and a bash description streams without enabling expansion.
Read-card tests: the derivation and its declines, the call line, and the ReadRow's collapse/open behaviour.
Search-card tests: the matches and paths derivations, the shape and argument validation, the recovery footer, and the SearchRow's presentation.
Spill-policy tests: a notice-only result stays generic while a result that fits keeps its terminal card.
Terminal-card tests: the exit marker parse, the workdir normalisation including UNC, the persistent/spilled/background paths, and the BashRow's presentation.
Todo-history tests: a missing predecessor is repaired on prepend, earlier cards stay fixed after a later write, and snapshots are immutable.
Todo row tests: the plan summary halves, the generic fallback on malformed args, the read-only checklist body, and the keyed registration.
ToolCallTree tests: only the changed child of 100 siblings dispatches, the disclosure hook resets, the DOM anchors hold, and an Auto denial renders generically.
Shared fixtures building the canonical Chat slice and the matching Session event window for the Tool row tests.
CSS assertions for the summary line: the suffix stays on one line and unshrunk, and the summary text alone carries the truncation.
The row-model and ToolRow contract: classification, titles, summaries, state derivation, the file link, the error line, the suffix, the diff totals, and the IO card gutters.
The keyed toolview hole through the real machinery: dispatch by entry key, the generic fallback, the Auto denial, the file-open path to the Sidebar, and live registration takeover.
Compile-time negative samples for the toolview slot types.
Web-card tests: the search and fetch derivations, the open-root argument validation, the href reader, and the WebRow's new-tab link.

Client tsconfig with 16 project references (spill-policy, attachment, remotes, workspace-controller, cordis, connection, locale, ui-chat, ui-conversation, primitives, renderer, session, slots, tools, user-questions, workspace-path).
Bundle config: the shared clientBundle helper with the type entry as the extra output.
